sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Richard Walter Burton (; né Jenkins Jr.; 10 November 1925 – 5 August 1984) was a Welsh actor.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Noted for his powerful presence and baritone voice, Burton had an expansive film and stage career.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He made his feature film debut in the British drama The Last Days of Dolwyn in 1949 and gained attention for his role as Philip Ashley, the protagonist in the romantic mystery My Cousin Rachel earning his first Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: On stage, Burton established himself as a Shakespearean actor, starring in roles such as roles such as Prince Hal in Henry IV, Part 1 (1951) and Henry IV, Part 2 (1951), Henry V of England in Henry V (1951), Ferdinand in The Tempest (1951), Prince Hamlet in Hamlet (1953), Sir Toby Belch in Twelfth Night (1953), Gnaeus Marcius Coriolanus in Coriolanus (1953), and Othello in Othello (1955).

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He was called "the natural successor to Olivier" by critic Kenneth Tynan.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Burton's perceived failure to live up to those expectations disappointed some critics and colleagues; his heavy drinking added to his reputation as a great performer who had wasted his talent.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Throughout his career Burton received numerous accolades, including a BAFTA Award, a Golden Globe Award and a Grammy Award.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He received the Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical for his portrayal of King Arthur in the Lerner and Loewe musical Camelot (1960).

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Despite seven Academy Award nominations Burton failed to win an Oscar; he was nominated for his performances in My Cousin Rachel (1952), The Robe (1953), Becket (1964), The Spy Who Came In from the Cold (1965), Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: (1966), Anne of the Thousand Days (1969) and Equus (1977).

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Burton has remained closely associated in the public mind with his second and third wife, Elizabeth Taylor due to their publicly turbulent relationship, in which they married and divorced twice, and starred in eleven films together.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Burton was born Richard Walter Jenkins Jr. on 10 November 1925 in a house at 2 Dan-y-bont in Pontrhydyfen, Glamorgan, Wales.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: He was the twelfth of thirteen children born into the Welsh-speaking family of Richard Walter Jenkins Sr. (5 March 1876 – 25 March 1957), and Edith Maude Jenkins (née Thomas; 28 January 1883 – 31 October 1927).

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Jenkins Sr., called Daddy Ni by the family, was a coal miner, while his mother worked as a barmaid at a pub called the Miners Arms in the village where she met her husband.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: They married, without approval of her parents, at Neath Register Office on 24 December 1900.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Biographer Melvyn Bragg quoted Burton as saying that Daddy Ni was a "twelve-pints-a-day man" who sometimes went off on drinking and gambling sprees for weeks, and that "he looked very much like me".

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Jenkins Sr. was badly burned in a mining explosion.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: His father, Thomas Jenkins, also a miner, had also had a serious mining accident and had relied on a wheelchair.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Burton described his mother as "a very strong woman" and "a religious soul with fair hair and a beautiful face".

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: But he was not quite two years old when she died on 31 October 1927, six days after the birth of Graham Jenkins, the family's thirteenth child.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Edith's death was a result of postpartum infections; Burton believed it had occurred because of "hygiene neglect".

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: According to biographer Michael Munn, Edith "was fastidiously clean", but her exposure to the dust from the coal mines resulted in her death.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Following Edith's death, Richard's elder sister Cecilia, whom he affectionately addressed as "Cis", and her husband Elfed James, also a miner, took him under their care until the age of seventeen.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Richard lived with Cis, Elfed and their two daughters, Marian and Rhianon, in their three-bedroom terraced cottage on 73 Caradoc Street, Taibach, a suburban district in Port Talbot, which Bragg describes as "a tough steel town, English-speaking, grind and grime".

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Burton remained grateful and loving to Cis throughout his life, later going on to say: "When my mother died she, my sister, had become my mother, and more mother to me than any mother could ever have been ...

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: I was immensely proud of her ... she felt all tragedies except her own".

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Daddy Ni would occasionally visit the homes of his grown daughters but was otherwise absent.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Another important figure in Richard's early life was Ifor, his brother, 19 years his senior.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: A miner and rugby union player, Ifor "ruled the household with the proverbial firm hand".

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: He was also responsible for nurturing a passion for rugby in young Richard.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Although Richard also played cricket, tennis, and table tennis, biographer Bragg notes rugby union football to be his greatest interest.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: On rugby, Burton said he "would rather have played for Wales at Cardiff Arms Park than Hamlet at The Old Vic".

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: The Welsh rugby union centre, Bleddyn Williams, believed the young Richard "had distinct possibilities as a player".

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: From the age of five to eight, Richard Jenkins was educated at the Eastern Primary School in Port Talbot, and he attended the boys' segment of the same school from eight to twelve years old.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: In March 1937, he took and passed a scholarship exam for admission into Port Talbot Secondary School Biographer Hollis Alpert notes that both Daddy Ni and Ifor considered Richard's education to be "of paramount importance" and planned to send him to the University of Oxford.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: Richard became the first member of his family to go to secondary school.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: He displayed an excellent speaking and singing voice from childhood, even winning an eisteddfod prize as a boy soprano.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: While a pupil at Port Talbot Secondary School, Richard also showed immense interest in reading poetry as well as English and Welsh literature.

sentences.section: Childhood
sentences.text: He earned pocket money by running messages, hauling horse manure, and delivering newspapers.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: In 1939, Richard was bolstered by winning a certificate at Maesteg Town Hall during a local eisteddfod and wanted to repeat his success.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: He chose to sing Sir Arthur Sullivan's "Orpheus with his Lute" (1866), which biographer Alpert thought "a difficult composition".

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: He requested the help of his schoolmaster, Philip Burton, but his voice cracked during their practice sessions.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: This incident marked the beginning of his association with Philip.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: Philip later recalled, "His voice was tough to begin with but with constant practice it became memorably beautiful."

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: Richard made his first foray into theatre with a minor role in his school's production of the Irish playwright George Bernard Shaw's The Apple Cart.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: He decided to leave school by the end of 1941 and work as a miner like Elfed.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: However, he ended up with a job, which he came to dislike intensely, at the local Taibach Co-operative retail store as a draper's assistant in the menswear department, limited at that time by war-time rationing.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: He also simultaneously considered other professions for his future, including boxing, religious ministry and singing.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: It was also during this period that Richard took up smoking and drinking despite being underage.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: When he joined the Port Talbot Squadron 499 of the Air Training Corps section of the Royal Air Force (RAF) as a cadet, he re-encountered Philip, who was the squadron commander.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: He also joined the Taibach Youth Centre, a youth drama group founded by Meredith Jones and led by Leo Lloyd, a steel worker and avid amateur thespian, who taught him the fundamentals of acting.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: Richard played the role of an escaped convict in Lloyd's play, The Bishop's Candlesticks, an adaptation of a section of Victor Hugo's Les Misérables.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: The play did not have any dialogue, but Alpert noted that Richard "mimed his role".

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: Philip gave him a part in a radio documentary/adaptation of his play for BBC Radio, Youth at the Helm (1942).

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: Seeing the talent Richard possessed, both Jones and Philip re-admitted him to school on 5 October 1942.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: Philip tutored his charge intensely in school subjects and also worked at developing the youth's acting voice, including outdoor voice drills which improved his projection.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: Richard called the experience "the most hardworking and painful period" in his life.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: Philip called Richard "my son to all intents and purposes.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: I was committed to him", while Burton later wrote of Philip, "I owe him everything".

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: In March 1943, aged 17, Richard left his sister's home as a result of his brother-in-law's resentment at supporting his resumed education.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: He sought the help of Philip Burton, who arranged his transfer to the home of widow Elizabeth 'Ma' Smith where he himself lodged.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: By the autumn of that year Philip planned to adopt Richard but was not able to do so as he was 20 days too young to be 21 years older than his adoptee, a legal requirement.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: As a result, with consent of his father, Richard became Philip's legal ward and, just aged 18, changed his surname on 26 November 1943 to "Burton", after Philip's own surname, by means of deed poll.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: It was also in 1943 that Richard qualified for admission into a university after excelling in the School Certificate Examination.

sentences.section: Philip Burton years
sentences.text: Philip requested Richard to study at Exeter College, Oxford, as a part of a six-month scholarship programme offered by the RAF for qualified cadets prior to active service.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: In 1943, Burton played Professor Henry Higgins in a school production of another Shaw play directed by Philip, Pygmalion.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: The role won him favourable reviews and caught the attention of the dramatist, Emlyn Williams, who offered Burton a small role as the lead character's elder brother, Glan, in his play The Druid's Rest.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: The play debuted at the Royal Court Theatre, Liverpool on 22 November 1943, and later premiered in St Martin's Theatre, London in January 1944.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: Burton thought the role was "a nothing part" and that he "hardly spoke at all".

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: He was paid ten pounds a week for playing the role (), which was "three times what the miners got".

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: Alpert states that the play garnered mixed critical reviews, but James Redfern of the New Statesman took notice of Burton's performance and wrote: "In a wretched part, Richard Burton showed exceptional ability."

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: Burton noted that single sentence from Redfern changed his life.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: While an undergraduate at Exeter College, University of Oxford, Burton featured as "the complicated sex-driven puritan" Angelo in the Oxford University Dramatic Society's 1944 production of William Shakespeare's Measure for Measure.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: The play was directed by Burton's English literature professor, Nevill Coghill, and was performed at the college in the presence of additional contributors to West End theatre including John Gielgud, Terence Rattigan and Binkie Beaumont.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: On Burton's performance, fellow actor and friend, Robert Hardy recalled, "There were moments when he totally commanded the audience by this stillness.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: And the voice which would sing like a violin and with a bass that could shake the floor."

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: Gielgud appreciated Burton's performance and Beaumont, who knew about Burton's work in The Druid's Rest, suggested that he "look him up" after completing his service in the RAF if he still wanted to pursue acting as a profession.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: In late 1944, Burton successfully completed his six-month scholarship at Exeter College, Oxford, and went to the RAF classification examinations held in Torquay to train as a pilot.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: He was disqualified for pilot training because his eyesight was below par, and was classified as a navigator trainee.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: He had a short term posting for training at a temporary RCAF training base in Carberry, Manitoba.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: He served in the RAF for three years, during which time rather than flight crew he was assigned as an Aircraftman 1st Class to perform an administrative role in a Wiltshire-based RAF Hospital, RAF Wroughton.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: Burton's habits of drinking and smoking increased during this period; he was involved in a brief casual affair with actress Eleanor Summerfield.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: Burton was cast in an uncredited and unnamed role of a bombing officer by BBC Third Programme in a 1946 radio adaptation of In Parenthesis, an epic poem of the First World War by David Jones.

sentences.section: 1943–1947: Early career and service in the RAF
sentences.text: Burton was discharged from the RAF on 16 December 1947.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: In 1948, Burton moved to London to make contact with H. M. Tennent Ltd., where he again met Beaumont, who put him under a contract of £500 per year (£10 a week).

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Daphne Rye, the casting director for H. M. Tennent Ltd., offered Burton rooms on the top floor of her house in Pelham Crescent, London as a place for him to stay.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Rye cast Burton in a minor role as a young officer, Mr. Hicks, in Castle Anna (1948), a drama set in Ireland.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: While touring with the cast and crew members of Wynyard Browne's Dark Summer, Burton was called by Emlyn Williams for a screen test for his film, The Last Days of Dolwyn (1949).

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Burton performed the screen test for the role of Gareth, which Williams wrote especially for him, and was subsequently selected when Williams sent him a telegram that quoted a line from The Corn Is Green — "You have won the scholarship."

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: This led to Burton making his mainstream film debut.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Filming took place during the summer and early autumn months of 1948.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: It was on the sets of this film that Burton was introduced by Williams to Sybil Williams, whom he married on 5 February 1949 at a registry office in Kensington.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: The Last Days of Dolwyn opened to generally positive critical reviews.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Burton was praised for his "acting fire, manly bearing and good looks" and film critic Philip French of The Guardian called it an "impressive movie debut".

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: After marrying Sybil, Burton moved into a flat at 6 Lyndhurst Road, Hampstead NW3, where he lived from 1949 to 1956.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Pleased with the feedback Burton received for his performance in The Last Days of Dolwyn, the film's co-producer Alexander Korda offered him a contract at a stipend of £100 a week (), which he signed.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: The contract allowed Korda to lend Burton to films produced by other companies.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Throughout the late 1940s and early 1950s, Burton acted in small parts in various British films such as Now Barabbas (1949) with Richard Greene and Kathleen Harrison, The Woman with No Name (1950) opposite Phyllis Calvert, and Waterfront (1950) with Harrison.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Burton had a bigger part as Robert Hammond, a spy for a newspaper editor in Green Grow the Rushes (1951) alongside Honor Blackman.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: His performance in Now Barabbas received positive feedback from critics.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: C. A. Lejeune of The Observer believed Burton had "all the qualities of a leading man that the British film industry badly needs at this juncture: youth, good looks, a photogenic face, obviously alert intelligence and a trick of getting the maximum effort with the minimum of fuss."

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: For The Woman With No Name, a critic from The New York Times thought Burton "merely adequate" in his role of the Norwegian aviator, Nick Chamerd.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Biographer Bragg states the reviews for Burton's performance in Waterfront were "not bad", and that Green Grow the Rushes was a box office bomb.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Rye recommended Richard to director Peter Glenville for the part of Hephaestion in Rattigan's play about Alexander the Great, Adventure Story, in 1949.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: The play was directed by Glenville and starred the then up-and-coming actor Paul Scofield as the titular character.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Glenville, however, rejected him as he felt that Burton was too short compared to Scofield.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Rye came to the rescue again by sending Burton to audition for a role in The Lady's Not for Burning, a play by Christopher Fry and directed by Gielgud.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: The lead roles were played by Gielgud himself, and Pamela Brown, while Burton played a supporting role as Richard alongside the then-relatively unknown actress Claire Bloom.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Gielgud was initially uncertain about selecting Burton and asked him to come back the following day to repeat his audition.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Burton got the part the second time he auditioned for the role.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: He was paid £15 a week for the part, which was five more than what Beaumont was paying him.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: After getting the part, he pushed for a raise in his salary from £10 to £30 a week with Williams' assistance, in addition to the £100 Korda paid him; Beaumont accepted it after much persuasion.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Bloom was impressed with Burton's natural way of acting, noting that "he just was" and went further by saying "He was recognisably a star, a fact he didn't question."

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: The play opened at the Globe Theatre in May 1949 and had a successful run in London for a year.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Writer and journalist Samantha Ellis of The Guardian, in her overview of the play, thought critics found Burton to be "most authentic" for his role.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Gielgud took the play to Broadway in the United States, where it opened at the Royale Theatre on 8 November 1950.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Theatre critic Brooks Atkinson appreciated the performances and praised the play's "hard glitter of wit and skepticism", while describing Fry as precocious with "a touch of genius".

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: The play ran on Broadway until 17 March 1951, and received the New York Drama Critics' Circle award for the Best Foreign Play of 1951.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Burton received the Theatre World Award for his performance, his first major award.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Burton went on to feature in two more plays by Fry – The Boy With A Cart and A Phoenix Too Frequent.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: The former opened at the Lyric Theatre, Hammersmith in February 1950, while the latter premiered at the Dolphin Theatre, Brighton the following month.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Gielgud, who also directed The Boy With A Cart, said that Burton's role in the play "was one of the most beautiful performances" he had ever seen.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: During its month-long run, Anthony Quayle, who was looking for a young actor to star as Prince Hal in his adaptations of Henry IV, Part I and Henry IV, Part 2 as a part of the Shakespeare Memorial Theatre season for the Festival of Britain, came to see the play and as soon as he beheld Burton, he realised he had found his man and got his agreement to play the parts.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Both plays opened in 1951 at the Shakespeare Memorial Theatre in Stratford-upon-Avon to mixed reviews, but Burton received acclaim for his role as Prince Hal, with many critics dubbing him "the next Laurence Olivier".

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Theatre critic Kenneth Tynan said of his performance, "His playing of Prince Hal turned interested speculation to awe almost as soon as he started to speak; in the first intermission local critics stood agape in the lobbies."

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: He was also praised by Humphrey Bogart and his wife Lauren Bacall after both saw the play.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Bacall later said of him: "He was just marvellous [...]

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Bogie loved him.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: We all did."

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Burton celebrated his success by buying his first car, a Standard Flying Fourteen, and enjoyed a drink with Bogart at a pub called The Dirty Duck.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Philip too was happy with the progress his ward made, and felt "proud, humble, and awed by god's mysterious ways".

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Burton went on to perform in Henry V as the titular character, and played Ferdinand in The Tempest as a part of the Shakespeare Memorial Theatre season as well.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: Neither role was overwhelmingly received by the critics, with a reviewer saying "he lacked inches" as Henry V. Olivier defended Burton by retaliating that he too received the same kind of review by the same critic for the same role.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: His last play in 1951 was as a musician named Orphée in Jean Anouilh's Eurydice opposite Dorothy McGuire and fellow Welsh actor Hugh Griffith.

sentences.section: 1948–1951: Rise through the ranks and film debut
sentences.text: The play, retitled as Legend of Lovers, opened in the Plymouth Theatre, New York City and ran for only a week, but critics were kind to Burton, with Bob Francis of Billboard magazine finding him "excellent as the self-tortured young accordionist".

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: Burton began 1952 by starring alongside Noel Willman in the title role of Emmanuel Roblès adventure Montserrat, which opened on 8 April at the Lyric Hammersmith.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: The play only ran for six weeks but Burton once again won praise from critics.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: According to Bragg, some of the critics who watched the performance considered it to be Burton's "most convincing role" till then.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: Tynan lauded Burton's role of Captain Montserrat, noting that he played it "with a variousness which is amazing when you consider that it is really little more than a protracted exposition of smouldering dismay".

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: Burton successfully made the transition to Hollywood on the recommendation of film director George Cukor when he was given the lead role in the Gothic romance film, My Cousin Rachel (1952) opposite Olivia de Havilland.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: Darryl F. Zanuck, co-founder of 20th Century Fox, negotiated a deal with Korda to lend Burton to the company for three films as well as pay Burton a total of $150,000 ($50,000 per film).

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: De Havilland did not get along well with Burton during filming, calling him "a coarse-grained man with a coarse-grained charm and a talent not completely developed, and a coarse-grained which makes him not like anyone else".

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: One of Burton's friends opined it may have been because of Burton's making remarks to her that she did not find in good taste.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: Based on the 1951 novel of the same name by Daphne du Maurier, My Cousin Rachel is about a man who suspects his rich cousin was murdered by his wife in order to inherit his wealth, but ends up falling in love with her, despite his suspicions.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: Upon release, the film was successful at the box office, and Burton's performance received mostly excellent reviews.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: Bosley Crowther, writing for The New York Times, appreciated Burton's emotional performance, describing it as "most fetching"; he called him "the perfect hero of Miss du Maurier's tale".

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: The Los Angeles Daily News reviewer stated "young Burton registers with an intense performance that stamps him as an actor of great potential".

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: Conversely, a critic from the Los Angeles Examiner labelled Burton as "terribly, terribly tweedy".

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: The film earned Burton the Golden Globe Award for New Star of the Year – Actor and his first Academy Award nomination in the Best Supporting Actor category.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: While shooting My Cousin Rachel, Burton was offered the role of Mark Antony in Julius Caesar (1953) by the production company, Metro Goldwyn Mayer (MGM), but Burton refused it to avoid schedule conflicts.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: The role subsequently went to Marlon Brando for which he earned a BAFTA Award for Best Foreign Actor and an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: The year 1953 marked an important turning point in Burton's career.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: He arrived in Hollywood at a time when the studio system was struggling.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic
sentences.text: The rise of television was drawing viewers away and the studios looked to new stars and film technologies to tempt viewers back to cinemas.

sentences.section: 1952–1954: Hollywood and The Old Vic

sentences.text: Burton was married five times, twice consecutively to Taylor.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: From 1949 until 1963, he was married to Sybil Williams, with whom he had two daughters, Kate (born 1957) and Jessica Burton (born 1959).

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: During the marriage Burton had a long affair with actress Claire Bloom.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: Burton told biographer Michael Munn "'I only ever loved two women before Elizabeth,' Sybil was one, Claire Bloom the other."

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: Burton's marriages to Taylor lasted from 15 March 1964 to 26 June 1974 and from 10 October 1975 to 29 July 1976.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: Their first wedding was at the Ritz-Carlton Hotel in Montreal.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: Of their marriage, Taylor proclaimed, "I'm so happy you can't believe it.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: This marriage will last forever."

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: Their second wedding took place 16 months after their divorce, in Chobe National Park in Botswana.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: Taylor and Eddie Fisher had adopted a daughter from Germany, Maria McKeown (born 1961), who was re-adopted by Burton after he and Taylor married.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: Burton also re-adopted Taylor and producer Mike Todd's daughter, Elizabeth Frances "Liza" Todd (born 1957), who had been first adopted by Fisher.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: The relationship Burton and Taylor portrayed in the film Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? was popularly likened to their real-life marriage.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: Burton disagreed with others about Taylor's famed beauty, saying that calling her "the most beautiful woman in the world is absolute nonsense.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: She has wonderful eyes, but she has a double chin and an overdeveloped chest, and she's rather short in the leg."

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: In August 1976, a month after his second divorce from Taylor, Burton married model Suzy Miller, the former wife of Formula 1 Champion James Hunt; the marriage ended in divorce in 1982.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: From 1983 until his death in 1984, Burton was married to a freelance production assistant Sally Hay.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: In 1974, between his divorce from and remarriage to Taylor, he was briefly engaged to Princess Elizabeth of Yugoslavia.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: In 1957, Burton had earned a total of £82,000 from Prince of Players, The Rains of Ranchipur and Alexander the Great, but only managed to keep £6,000 for personal expenses due to taxation imposed by the then-ruling Conservative government.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: As a result of a suggestion by his lawyer Aaron Frosch that he move to Switzerland, where the tax rate was lower, Burton moved with Sybil in January 1957 to Céligny, Switzerland, where he purchased a villa.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: In response to criticism from the British government, Burton remarked: "I believe that everyone should pay them — except actors."

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: Burton lived there until his death.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: In 1968, Burton's elder brother, Ifor, slipped and fell, breaking his neck, after a lengthy drinking session with Burton in Céligny.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: The injury left him paralysed from the neck down.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: His younger brother Graham Jenkins speculated that guilt over this may have caused Burton to start drinking very heavily, particularly after Ifor died in 1972.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: In a February 1975 interview with his friend David Lewin, he said he "tried" homosexuality.

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: He also suggested that perhaps all actors were latent homosexuals, and "we cover it up with drink".

sentences.section: Marriages and relationships
sentences.text: In 2000, Ellis Amburn's biography of Elizabeth Taylor suggested that Burton had an affair with Laurence Olivier and tried to seduce Eddie Fisher, although this was strongly denied by Burton's younger brother Graham Jenkins.

sentences.text: Burton admired and was inspired by the actor and dramatist Emlyn Williams.

sentences.section: Personal views
sentences.text: Politically, Burton was a lifelong socialist, although he was never as heavily involved in politics as his close friend Stanley Baker.

sentences.section: Personal views
sentences.text: He admired Democratic senator Robert F. Kennedy and once got into a sonnet-quoting contest with him.

sentences.section: Personal views
sentences.text: In 1972, Burton played Leon Trotsky in The Assassination of Trotsky.

sentences.section: Personal views
sentences.text: The next year, he agreed to play Josip Broz Tito in a film biography, since he admired the Yugoslav leader.

sentences.section: Personal views
sentences.text: While filming in Yugoslavia he publicly proclaimed that he was a communist, saying he felt no contradiction between earning vast sums of money for films and holding left-wing views since "unlike capitalists, I don't exploit other people".

sentences.section: Personal views
sentences.text: In November 1974, Burton was banned permanently from BBC productions for writing two newspaper articles questioning the sanity of Winston Churchill and others in power during World War II.

sentences.section: Personal views
sentences.text: Burton reported hating them "virulently" for the alleged promise to wipe out all Japanese people on the planet.

sentences.section: Personal views
sentences.text: The publication of these articles coincided with what would have been the 100th year since Churchill's birth and came after Burton had played him in a favourable light in A Walk with Destiny.

sentences.section: Personal views
sentences.text: On his religious views, Burton was an atheist, stating: "I wish I could believe in a God of some kind but I simply cannot."

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: Burton was a heavy smoker.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: In a December 1977 interview with Sir Ludovic Kennedy, Burton said he was smoking 60–100 cigarettes per day.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: According to his younger brother, as stated in Graham Jenkins's 1988 book Richard Burton: My Brother, he smoked at least 100 cigarettes a day.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: After his father died from a cerebral haemorrhage in March 1957, Burton declined to attend his funeral.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: Burton was also an alcoholic most of his adult life.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: According to biographer Robert Sellers, "At the height of his boozing in the mid-70s he was knocking back three to four bottles of hard liquor a day."

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: After nearly drinking himself to death during the shooting of The Klansman (1974), Burton dried out at Saint John's Health Center in Santa Monica, California.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: Burton was allegedly inebriated while making the movie, and many of his scenes had to be filmed with him sitting or lying down due to his inability to stand upright.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: In some scenes, he appears to slur his words or speak incoherently.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: Burton later said that he could not remember making the film.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: Co-star O. J. Simpson said "There would be times when he couldn't move".

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: According to his diaries, Burton used Antabuse to try to stop his excessive consumption of alcohol, which he blamed for wrecking his marriage to Taylor.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: Burton himself said of the time leading up to his near loss of life, "I was fairly sloshed for five years.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: I was up there with John Barrymore and Robert Newton.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: The ghosts of them were looking over my shoulder."

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: He said that he turned to the bottle for solace "to burn up the flatness, the stale, empty, dull deadness that one feels when one goes offstage".

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: The 1988 biography by Melvyn Bragg provides a detailed description of the many health issues that plagued Burton throughout his life.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: In his youth, Burton had been known for being exceptionally strong and athletic.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: By the age of 41, he had declined so far in health that by his own admission, his arms were thin and weak.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: He suffered from bursitis, possibly aggravated by faulty treatment, arthritis, dermatitis, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease, as well as developing, by his mid-forties, a pronounced limp.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: How much of this was due to his intake of alcohol is impossible to ascertain, according to Bragg, because of Burton's reluctance to be treated for alcoholism.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: In 1974, Burton spent six weeks in a clinic to recuperate from a period during which he had drunk three bottles of vodka a day.

sentences.section: Health problems
sentences.text: Health issues continued to plague him until his death.

sentences.section: Declining health and death
sentences.text: Burton died from intracerebral haemorrhage at his home in Céligny, Switzerland, on 5 August 1984, aged 58.

sentences.section: Declining health and death
sentences.text: Although his death was sudden, his health had been declining for several years, and he suffered from constant and severe neck pain.

sentences.section: Declining health and death
sentences.text: As early as March 1970, he had been warned that his liver was enlarged, and he was diagnosed with cirrhosis and kidney disease in April 1981.

sentences.section: Declining health and death
sentences.text: Burton was buried at the Old Cemetery (Vieux Cimetière) of Céligny with a copy of Dylan Thomas's poems.

sentences.section: Declining health and death
sentences.text: Burton left an estate worth US$4.58 million ().

sentences.section: Declining health and death
sentences.text: The bulk of his estate consisted of real estate, investments in three countries, and works of art.

sentences.section: Declining health and death
sentences.text: Most of his estate was bequeathed to his widow, Sally Hay.
